title: Commit an atomic score edit input
description: One atomic compare-and-swap command shared by desktop and MCP. Authenticate the actor externally. Selection score/revision and expected_revision_id must agree and equal current head at commit. Resolve the immutable selection reference, never its original query against a new head. Apply operations to a private working revision and publish all or none. Unknown caller authority/provenance fields are rejected.

common__Id.description: Opaque stable external identifier. A displayed measure number, staff number, or event ordinal is not an identifier. External IDs are not automatically legal SFS aliases: use the returned alias/reference map and TextIdentifier for fragment-local names.

common__PositiveRational.description: Strictly positive canonical rational; requires the same reduction check as Rational.

common__Rational.description: Exact canonical rational in quarter-note units where applicable. Integers have no denominator; fractions have positive denominator > 1. Semantic validation additionally requires gcd(abs(n), d)=1. JSON Schema alone cannot enforce reduction; 2/4 is rejected by the semantic validator. No floating-point JSON values, leading zeros, -0, 0/d, or n/1.

common__RevisionId.description: Immutable score revision identifier; never the mutable alias latest.

common__TextIdentifier.description: SFS lexical identifier used for a fragment-local voice alias or event ID. It is distinct from an opaque external score/revision/object identifier. The parser and returned binding map establish correspondence.

common__WrittenPitch.description: Canonical written pitch, e.g. C4, Db4, C##4, C(+1/2)4. Semantic checks enforce reduced alterations and the short forms for 0, +/-1 and +/-2 semitones. This is a spelling, not a printed accidental or a MIDI value.

edit__DeleteEvents.description: Delete named events and score-owned attached marks. Delete a relation only when all of its referenced members are deleted. Any surviving dependent endpoint/member requires an explicit relation operation in this same transaction. Future knowledge annotations are not score-owned marks and are never deleted here.

edit__IdentityReplacement.description: Explicit replacement lineage, not a claim of unchanged semantic identity. Old and new IDs remain distinct. Future follow-identity annotations require review for a replacement even when lineage exists.

edit__MoveEvent.description: Move an existing event in its existing clock; optionally change voice/staff. Preserve identity, pitch and duration. The destination must be an explicitly selected scope, existing staff must belong to the destination part, and no dependent relation may be left unresolved. Cross-clock moves are unsupported.

oneOf.description: Reference an explicitly named event inside the replace_range operation at this zero-based index in the same transaction. The command authority allocates final identities and resolves this reference before final graph validation; never guess a future global ID.

edit__RemoveRelation.description: Explicitly remove this score relation. It must be internal to, or appear in the frozen selection's touching context. Report impacts outside the selected notes; never infer this operation from a dangling endpoint.

edit__ReplaceRange.description: Replace selected voices only inside the frozen span. Parse !fragment 1.1 unit=q span=<length>, local committed @frames and !end at=<length>; no !part declarations. Span length equals end-start and is preserved exactly. Bind aliases explicitly. v1.1 fragments carry event/mark/relation edits only: they cannot introduce persistent state or change measure-boundary objects. Existing states and measure objects stay at their frozen positions; inserted events are validated against that preserved context at every onset. Notes crossing either outer boundary are rejected rather than silently cut. Untouched spanning relations remain intact; affected external endpoints/members need explicit relation operations in the same atomic transaction. Ripple is unsupported and not advertised.

edit__ReplacementSpan.description: Half-open target span. Must exactly match one frozen contiguous time/measure span and the explicitly affected voices. An arbitrary event-set bounding box is not replaceable. All selected local measure boundaries and unsupported state boundaries must be aligned or the operation is rejected.

edit__RetargetRelation.description: Explicitly retarget a registered endpoint role of an existing relation to an existing or same-transaction fragment event. Only relation kinds whose registry defines that endpoint role support this operation; non-binary/member-based relations require a dedicated future operation. Validate kind, scope, order and musical constraints against the final transaction graph.

edit__SetDuration.description: Change one ordinary timed note/rest/spacer duration and its explicitly supplied written-duration fields; no ripple and no automatic split. Grace and open-duration event kinds reject this operation. The event must remain within the frozen editing scope and score extent.

edit__SetPitch.description: Change one pitched event's written pitch. Onset, duration, voice and staff are unchanged. preserve_if_consistent rejects contradictory existing explicit accidentals; recompute is an explicit engraving request and must report all resulting accidental-object changes. Tied endpoints and transposition-dependent constraints are validated at transaction end.

edit__TimeModification.description: Per-event written time modification, distinct from visible tuplet relations. Optional normal_type/normal_dots are preserved when explicitly supplied.

edit__VoiceBinding.description: Map a fragment-local alias to one pre-existing logical voice identity in the selected revision. Use the returned mapping; never paste an opaque voice ID into SFS as if it were an alias.

edit__WrittenDuration.description: Explicit replacement of this event's written duration fields. The engine verifies consistency with the requested exact duration; it never silently changes onsets, unrelated events or measure lengths.

selection__FrozenSelectionRef.description: Reference to an immutable, server-resolved selection. All three components must agree. Never re-evaluate against a newer head.
